thread:
Elena (Design): Thinking out loud: what if we surface 1-3 'priority permissions' as a horizontal strip next to the role name, then collapse the rest into a compact grid that expands. Mock: https://staging.redwood.design/perm-strip-v1 :sparkles:
Asha (PM): Goal is quick scanability. Most orgs check 3 things: billing, remove members, manage apps. If those are visible instantly it's huge. But we need to avoid ambiguous labels.
Noah (Engineer): Technical concerns: rendering performance with 500+ roles. Virtualize rows and avoid heavy DOM for tooltips. Also avoid hover-only reveal.
Priya (UX Research): In hallway testing people misinterpreted icons without text. Recommend small verb-based microcopy ("Manage billing", "Remove members") under icons.
Elena (Design): Updated idea: chips with icon + 1-line verb. Secondary grid uses single-letter compact toggles with accessible labels. Add a persistent legend above with examples.
Lee (Frontend): Accessibility callouts: chips should be buttons with aria-pressed states. Use aria-label="Manage billing permission: enabled for role X" for screen readers. Also ensure focus-visible styles.
Asha (PM): Copy: avoid "Admin" as it's overloaded. Use task-based labels. Also for invites flow, mention default role clearly: "Default role for invites" and add a link to change defaults.
Noah (Engineer): For audit nav, propose a deep link pattern: /orgs/{org}/audit?entity=role&entity_id={id}&filter=permission_change. We can wire a keyboard shortcut (press "/" then "a") to open audit filtered to focused role.
Priya (UX Research): Add test scenarios: find who can revoke access, find when billing permissions were granted, success path for inviting with custom role. Include keyboard-only and screen reader participants.
Elena (Design): Microcopy proposal: top of matrix show small help text: "High-priority permissions shown here; expand to edit full permission set." Keep it concise.
Lee (Frontend): CSS prototype for focus and reduced reliance on color:
```css
.priority-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items:center; gap:8px; padding:4px 8px; border-radius:6px; }
.priority-chip[aria-pressed="true"] { background: color(token-accent-subtle); }
.role-row:focus-within { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color(token-focus); }
```
Lee (Frontend): We'll map token names to accessible hex values.
Asha (PM): Invite UX: when selecting a default role, show a microcopy tooltip: "This role will be applied to people invited via links or email by default." Consider making default role selection part of org settings top-level panel.
Noah (Engineer): Performance note: server should return a "priority_permissions" array per role to avoid computing on client for large orgs. We'll add that field to the API v2.
Priya (UX Research): Observability: add an event when users expand a role (metrics: expand_role, role_id) to see if compactness reduces cognitive load.
Elena (Design): Accessibility extra: add visible focus target for the expand chevron and ensure expansion is preserved across pagination. Also keyboard aria-controls linking.
Asha (PM): Action items:
- @Lee: implement focus styles + chip semantics (ETA Tue)
- @Noah: API change for priority_permissions + audit deep-links (ETA next sprint)
- @Priya: recruit 6 admins + 3 screen reader users, write script (ETA Thu)
- @Elena: update frames with help text + legend and new microcopy (ETA Mon)
- @Asha: update invite settings copy and add default role CTA (ETA Wed)
